Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: George Borrow (author, Wikidata Q2137717), died 1881; Adam Mickiewicz (other, Wikidata Q79822), died 1855; Aleksandr Sergeevich Pushkin (other, Wikidata Q7200), died 1837. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Borrow, George, 1803-1881; Mickiewicz, Adam, 1798-1855 [Contributor]; Pushkin, Aleksandr Sergeevich, 1799-1837 [Contributor]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: Targum: or, Metrical translations from thirty languages and dialects. And The talisman, from the Russian of Alexander Pushkin. With other pieces, London, Jarrold & sons, 1892, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/cu31924013438183. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 84%, 67%, 93% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of George Borrow, Adam Mickiewicz, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
